blocks.text: An invitation to the Centre Pompidou on the occasion of the Bicentennial of Photography. Drawn from the Centre Pompidou’s photography collection, this display brings together around one hundred works by some thirty historical and contemporary artists, a large share of them recent acquisitions.

The thematic route through the display, conceived as a non-exhaustive tribute to the invention of photography on the occasion of its bicentennial, is organized around four main themes (“Making the Image,” “To Infinity,” “The Studio,” “Identities”). It takes a cross-cutting look at artistic practices based on photography, from the early 20th century to the present day.

Many artists, such as Robert Cumming, Sophie Thun and Kunié Sugiura, are fascinated by the ways of making images: they exploit the diversity of devices that record or generate images. Others, like Timm Ulrichs, Dinh Q Lê and Eileen Quinlan, explore the principle of reproduction at the heart of this medium. Their works speak to our interest in copies and replicas, just as they reveal our obsessive relationship to reality, and to its fantasized possession through the image. Another fundamental component of photography is its role in the construction of identities, notably through the development of portraiture and self-portraiture. These photographic genres, which Martha Wilson, Andrzej Steinbach and Sam Contis, among others, have made their own, have a rich and complex history, revealing the interplay of control and power exerted by the image in our societies.

Damarice Amao, Florian Ebner (respectively Curator and Head of the Photography Department, Centre Pompidou-Musée national d’art moderne) and Julie Jones (formerly a curator in the Photography Department at the Centre Pompidou and, since February 2026, Director of the Maison Européenne de la photographie).
